Emaar plans to offer 15 dirhams per share for the outstanding stake, valuing Emaar Development at $16.3bln

Federico Maccioni | Reuters News

DUBAI - Dubai's Emaar Properties aims to delist its construction arm Emaar Development from the local stock exchange, it said on Thursday, as its board approved plans to launch a buyout offer worth as much as $3.4 billion.

* The move follows a change of ownership this year at Emaar, developer of the world's tallest building, the Burj Khalifa

* Emaar plans to offer 15 dirhams per share for the outstanding stake, valuing Emaar Development at $16.3 billion

* The cash offer represents a 19.4% premium to Emaar Development's November 2 closing price of 12.56 dirhams per share

* The deal "would bring the UAE development business fully within the group, allowing it to be managed and funded under a single capital allocation framework," Emaar said

* Emaar Properties owns just over 79% of Emaar Development, while unit Emaar Property Holdings Limited (EPHL) holds a further 1%

* The Gulf is grappling with the turmoil of the US-Iran war, which has impacted sectors including travel and hospitality

* Still, Emaar on Thursday reported a 13% rise in revenue in the first nine months of the year, helped by construction progress and high occupancy across its shopping malls. It also approved a special dividend worth about $1.2 billion

* JPMorgan is acting as Emaar Properties' financial adviser, while Emirates NBD Capital is lead manager and FAB is co-lead manager

(Reporting by Federico Maccioni. Editing by Mark Potter)
